local_context.value: Sea Island in Beaufort County surrounded by expansive marshes, especially on the southeastern side; described as a major centre of African-American Gullah culture and language. Page gives no elevation, climate or housing data.

neighborhoods.value: Established communities Frogmore (commercial centre) and Lands End (also called Fort Fremont); other named areas Cedar Grove, Eddings Point, Coffin Point, Fripp Point, Warsaw Island, plus Dulamo Road, Folly Road and Pollawana Road areas. 7 named places plus 3 road-named areas; the page does not state town limits (island is not described as incorporated).

things_to_do.value: Penn Center — York W. Bailey Museum (16 Penn Center Circle West; 'Education for Freedom' exhibit on the Penn School; docent-led tours; hours change — no hours on the page); Penn Center Heritage Days, the annual celebration each November (no year's dates). Fort Fremont Preserve and History Center (county-owned, 1124 Land's End Road, fort built 1898) and the St. Helena Parish Chapel of Ease ruins (NRHP 1988, c. 1740, burned 1886; search summary only) are Top Sites, not repeated here.

top_sites.value: Fort Fremont (former military battery at Lands End guarding the Beaufort River entrance); Penn School/Penn Center (post-emancipation school for freed people, linked from page); National Register: Indian Hill Site, Knights of Wise Men Lodge.
